meta.name: LR Mate 200iD Robot
meta.summary: 6-axis, 7 kg payload, 717 mm reach robot on an R-30iB Mate Plus controller, set up to unload an injection molding machine through a Euromap 67 interface. Built from public FANUC documentation; cell-specific I/O is shown as a typical assignment to replace with your own. 3D model built on the published link lengths at the zero pose; housing shapes are approximate.

components.name: Robot riser / pedestal
components.desc: Steel riser bolted to the floor; sets the robot height to reach into the mold area. Cell-specific.

components.name: J1 base
components.desc: Fixed base of the robot. Holds the J1 motor and reducer, the robot connection cable entry and the Pulsecoder backup battery. Mounting face to J2 axis 330 mm; J1–J2 offset 50 mm.

parts.name: J1 servomotor with Pulsecoder and brake

components.name: J1 swivel (turntable)
components.desc: Rotates the arm about the vertical axis. J1 range up to 340° (360° option), max 450°/s.

components.name: J2 motor and reducer
components.desc: Servomotor with built-in Pulsecoder driving the lower arm (J2, max 380°/s).

components.name: J2 arm (lower arm)
components.desc: Lower arm between the J2 and J3 axes: 330 mm between axes.

components.name: J3 casing and J3 motor
components.desc: Elbow housing. Holds the J3 motor and reducer (J3 max 520°/s) and the rear of the J4–J6 drive train.

components.name: J3 arm (forearm) with J4
components.desc: Forearm that rotates about its own axis (J4, max 550°/s). Carries the wrist motors and the end-effector cabling. J3 offset 35 mm, J3 axis to wrist centre 335 mm.

components.name: Wrist unit (J5/J6)
components.desc: Wrist bend (J5, 545°/s) and faceplate rotation (J6, 1000°/s). Wrist load limits apply to the gripper's weight and offset. Wrist centre to faceplate 80 mm.

components.name: End-of-arm tool (gripper)
components.desc: Vacuum or finger gripper on the J6 faceplate, driven from the EE connector outputs and robot air ports. Cell-specific.

components.name: EE connector and air ports
components.desc: End-effector interface on the J3 casing: robot inputs/outputs (RI/RO), pneumatic pressure alarm input and air supply ports for the gripper.
components.src: B-83525EN (R-30iB Mate/Mate Plus maintenance manual) Part II §4

components.name: Robot connection cable
components.desc: Power, brake and Pulsecoder cable between the controller and the robot base (RMP1/RP1 type). Damage here causes DTERR/CRCERR and overtravel/hand-broken alarms.

components.name: R-30iB Mate Plus controller
components.desc: Controller cabinet: main board, 6-axis servo amplifier, power supply, E-stop unit and board, backplane, fans, breaker and discharge resistor.

components.name: Operator panel (mode switch, E-stop)
components.desc: Cabinet front: E-stop button, AUTO/T1/T2 mode switch, start and reset buttons and the CYCLE START lamp.

components.name: Teach pendant (iPendant)
components.desc: Teaching and operation. Has its own E-stop, the enabling (deadman) switch and the TP enable switch.

components.name: Safety fence and gate interlock
components.desc: Cell guarding. The gate switch wires to the fence (EAS) terminals; opening it in AUTO stops the robot with SRVO-004.

components.name: Molding machine interface (Euromap 67)
components.desc: Handshake between the robot and the molding machine: mold open, mold area free, ejector permits and the shared E-stop and safety circuit.

components.name: Part conveyor / drop-off
components.desc: Where the robot places parts. Cell-specific.

faults.title: Operator panel E-stop
causes: Cabinet E-stop button pressed
Broken wire or bad contact in the panel E-stop circuit
Faulty operator panel, E-stop board or main board
checks: Release the cabinet E-stop and press RESET
Check STATUS > Stop Signal: SOP E-Stop should read FALSE
Check the panel E-stop switch contacts and its connector
If SRVO-213 is also active, check the E-stop board fuse first
Back up the controller before replacing the main board

faults.title: Teach pendant E-stop
causes: Pendant E-stop button pressed
Faulty pendant or pendant cable
checks: Release the pendant E-stop and reset
If it won't clear, swap in a known-good pendant

faults.title: Deadman switch released
causes: Enabling switch released, or squeezed past the middle position, while the pendant is enabled
Mode switch or TP enable switch in the wrong position
Faulty pendant, mode switch or E-stop board
checks: Hold the enabling switch in its middle position and reset
Check that the TP enable switch matches the mode (ON for T1/T2)
Check STATUS > Stop Signal: TP Deadman and TP Enable

faults.title: Fence open
causes: Cell gate opened in AUTO mode
Gate switch out of adjustment or wiring open at the fence (EAS) terminals
Mode switch fault
checks: Close the gate and reset
Check the gate switch actuator alignment
Check continuity on the EAS terminals of the E-stop board
Never jumper the fence circuit to run production

faults.title: Robot overtravel
causes: An axis hit its overtravel limit switch
Limit switch faulty
Open fuse FS2 on the servo amplifier
Robot cable or EE connector damaged
checks: Use the overtravel release, then jog the axis back into range
Check fuse FS2 on the amplifier
Inspect the robot connection cable and EE connector for damage or pinching
faults.safety: Jog slowly after an overtravel release; soft limits are bypassed while recovering.

faults.title: Hand broken
causes: Gripper crash protector (safety joint) tripped
Hand-broken signal cable open or unplugged
Hand-broken input enabled but not wired
checks: Reset the crash protector and inspect the gripper for damage
Check the hand-broken cable at the EE connector
If the cell has no crash protector, check that the hand-broken input is disabled in setup

faults.title: External E-stop
causes: Cell E-stop (molding machine, conveyor, door) pressed
Open wire at the external E-stop (EES) terminals
E-stop board fault
checks: Release every cell E-stop and reset
Check the molding machine's E-stop chain through the Euromap 67 interface
Check continuity on the EES terminals
Never jumper the external E-stop circuit

faults.title: Pneumatic pressure alarm
causes: Low air pressure at the robot (pressure switch on the EE interface)
Air supply valve closed, filter blocked or hose cut
EE connector or robot cable fault
checks: Check the air supply pressure and the regulator for the cell
Inspect the gripper hoses for kinks or cuts
Check the pressure switch and its EE connector pin

faults.title: Cabinet fan stopped
causes: Backplane fan blocked or failed
Fan cable unplugged
checks: Inspect the fan for dirt or a stuck rotor and replace it
Check the fan connectors on the backplane
The robot stops about 1 minute after this alarm; fix it promptly
faults.safety: Lock out the controller before opening the cabinet; the amplifier DC bus can stay charged after power-off.

faults.title: System overheat
causes: Cabinet ambient above 45 °C
Fans failed or filters/vents blocked
Faulty thermostat on the main board
checks: Measure the air temperature around the cabinet
Clean the vents and heat exchanger; check that the fans run
The robot stops about 1 minute after this alarm

faults.title: Brake abnormal
causes: Excess brake current: shorted brake or brake cable
Brake release unit left connected and switched on
Servo amplifier fault
checks: Disconnect any brake release unit
Check the brake circuit in the robot cable for shorts
Replace the amplifier if the cable and motor check good
faults.safety: Support the arm before working on brakes: J2 and J3 can drop when a brake is released.

faults.title: SRDY off
causes: Servo amplifier did not become ready after the main contactor closed
Loose connector between the E-stop unit and the amplifier
Brief interruption of input power
E-stop unit or amplifier fault
checks: Check for an input power dip at the time of the alarm
Reseat the amplifier and E-stop unit connectors
Replace the E-stop unit, then the amplifier, if it repeats
faults.safety: Lock out the controller before opening the cabinet; the amplifier DC bus can stay charged after power-off.

faults.title: Stop or move error excess
faults.msg: Stop error excess / Move error excess / Inpos time over
causes: Brake not releasing on an axis
Collision or the arm is held or overloaded
Gripper heavier than the payload setting
Motor or amplifier fault; low input voltage
checks: Check that the payload schedule matches the real gripper and part
Check the axis for mechanical binding or a collision
Listen for the brake releasing when servos turn on
Check input voltage, then replace the motor or amplifier

faults.title: Robot not mastered
causes: Calibration attempted without valid mastering data
Quick mastering reference never set
checks: Master the robot (SYSTEM > Master/Cal), then calibrate
Set the quick-mastering reference position after a good mastering

faults.title: IMSTP input
causes: The *IMSTP UOP input from the cell PLC is off (normally-closed signal)
checks: Check the PLC is sending *IMSTP (UI[1]) ON
Check the UOP wiring and that UOP is enabled

faults.title: Pulse mismatch
causes: Encoder count changed while power was off (motor replaced, battery change, axis moved with the brake released)
Controller memory restored from another robot
checks: Check whether the brake was released or the arm moved while off
Re-master the affected axis
Replace the motor if it repeats with no cause

faults.title: DCAL (regeneration) alarm
causes: Too much regenerative energy: fast decelerations with a heavy load
Discharge resistor open or its fuse (FS3) blown
Cabinet fan clogged, input voltage high
checks: Reduce acceleration or duty on heavy moves
Check fuse FS3 and measure the discharge resistor (about 6.5 Ω)
Clean the fans and check input voltage
faults.safety: Lock out the controller before opening the cabinet; the amplifier DC bus can stay charged after power-off.

faults.title: High DC bus voltage (HVAL)
causes: Input voltage too high
Regeneration not absorbed (discharge resistor circuit)
checks: Measure the controller supply voltage
Check the discharge resistor circuit
Replace the amplifier if voltage and resistor are fine
faults.safety: Lock out the controller before opening the cabinet; the amplifier DC bus can stay charged after power-off.

faults.title: High current (HCAL)
causes: Short in the motor power wiring or motor winding
Amplifier power stage fault
checks: Disconnect the robot cable and see if the alarm clears (isolates amplifier vs. cable/motor)
Megger the power cable insulation and measure motor winding resistance
Replace the faulty part
faults.safety: Lock out the controller before opening the cabinet; the amplifier DC bus can stay charged after power-off.

faults.title: Overcurrent (OVC)
causes: Motor current too high for too long: heavy load or high duty
Brake dragging
Mechanical binding, worn reducer
Low input voltage
checks: Check payload settings and reduce speed or duty
Check for binding by jogging slowly and watching the disturbance torque
Check brake release and input voltage
Do not relax the overload parameters to clear it

faults.title: Collision detect
causes: The arm or gripper hit something (often a part stuck in the mold)
Payload setting wrong
Brake dragging, low voltage, or reducer/balancer damage
checks: Check the gripper and the mold area for a collision and damage
Confirm the payload schedule matches the gripper and part
Check the position of the molding machine's ejector and slides before re-entering
Re-check TCP and mastering after a hard crash
faults.safety: Before entering the mold after a collision, lock out the molding machine as well as the robot.

faults.title: FSSB communication error
faults.msg: FSSB com error / disconnect / init error
causes: Optical fiber between the main board and amplifier dirty, bent or unplugged
Fuse FS1 on the amplifier blown
Servo card, amplifier or main board fault
Pulsecoder cable shorted to ground
checks: Check the fiber cable ends and bend radius
Check fuse FS1
Swap boards in order: servo card, amplifier, main board (back up first)
faults.safety: Lock out the controller before opening the cabinet; the amplifier DC bus can stay charged after power-off.

faults.title: Encoder battery lost (BZAL)
causes: Pulsecoder backup battery dead or disconnected while power was off
Battery cable broken
checks: Replace the battery pack in the robot base
Reset the Pulsecoder alarm ($MCR.$SPC_RESET), then cycle power
Re-master the robot: position data was lost
faults.safety: Change the Pulsecoder battery with the controller powered ON and the E-stop pressed, otherwise position data is lost.

faults.title: Encoder battery low (BLAL)
causes: Pulsecoder backup battery voltage below rating
checks: Replace the battery promptly with the controller ON and E-stop pressed
Waiting until the next power-off can turn this into a BZAL and force re-mastering

faults.title: Motor overheat (OHAL2)
causes: Motor thermostat tripped: long high-duty operation or heavy load
checks: Let the motor cool and retry
Reduce speed, duty or payload
Replace the motor if it trips at normal duty

faults.title: Encoder communication error
causes: Pulsecoder signal cable damaged, unplugged or poorly shielded
Electrical noise
Pulsecoder or amplifier fault
checks: Inspect the robot connection cable and its connectors at both ends
Check cable shield grounding
Replace the motor (Pulsecoder), cable or amplifier in turn

faults.title: Pulsecoder failure
causes: Pulsecoder internal fault
Noise on the encoder line (CMAL)
checks: For CMAL check grounding of the controller, cable and motor flange first
Replace the motor and re-master the axis

faults.title: Pulse not established
causes: Absolute position not yet established after a Pulsecoder reset or battery loss
checks: Reset the alarm and jog the axis slowly about one motor revolution until it clears

faults.title: Cabinet door open
causes: Controller cabinet door open, or door switch faulty
checks: Close and latch the door
Check the door switch and E-stop unit connectors

faults.title: E-stop board fuse blown
causes: A fuse on the E-stop board opened (usually 24 V shorted in the cell safety wiring)
checks: Check the E-stop board fuse whenever SRVO-213 shows with SRVO-001, -004 or -007
Find the short in the external E-stop or fence wiring before replacing the fuse
faults.safety: Lock out the controller before opening the cabinet; the amplifier DC bus can stay charged after power-off.

faults.title: Safety chain mismatch
causes: The two channels of an E-stop, fence or enable circuit did not switch together (worn contact, one wire open)
Deadman held at an in-between position
checks: Find the device that tripped by operating each E-stop and gate in turn
Check both channels of that device
Repair the fault, then clear it with the chain-failure reset on the alarm screen
faults.src: dual-channel safety practice; verify procedure in B-83284EN-1

faults.title: Teach pendant will not power on
causes: Fuse FUSE3 on the E-stop board blown (board LED red)
Pendant cable damaged
Pendant or E-stop board fault
checks: Check FUSE3 on the E-stop board
Inspect the pendant cable
Swap a known-good pendant, then replace the E-stop board
faults.safety: Lock out the controller before opening the cabinet; the amplifier DC bus can stay charged after power-off.

faults.title: Pendant stuck on the start-up screen
causes: Controller did not finish booting: main board, backplane or option board fault
Fuse FUSE1 on the main board blown
checks: Read the main board status and 7-segment LEDs and look them up
Check FUSE1 on the main board
Remove option boards one at a time to isolate
faults.safety: Lock out the controller before opening the cabinet; the amplifier DC bus can stay charged after power-off.

faults.title: Joint limit error
causes: A taught or calculated position is past an axis's software limit
checks: Check which axis is at its limit on the position screen
Reteach the point or change the wrist configuration
faults.src: general FANUC practice — verify in B-83284EN-1 alarm code list

faults.title: Position not reachable
causes: Target is outside the robot's reach, often after a user frame or tool frame change
checks: Check the active user and tool frame numbers
Reteach the point
faults.src: general FANUC practice — verify in B-83284EN-1 alarm code list

faults.title: Singularity
causes: J5 near 0° so J4 and J6 line up during a linear move
checks: Change the wrist orientation slightly, or use a joint move through that area
faults.src: general FANUC practice — verify in B-83284EN-1 alarm code list

faults.title: Robot will not start from the molding machine / PLC
causes: UOP not enabled, or *IMSTP, *HOLD, *SFSPD or ENBL inputs not ON
Robot not in AUTO, or the pendant still enabled
Program selection (RSR/PNS) not acknowledged
Euromap 67 robot-mode or safety signals missing
checks: Check the UOP screen: UI[1], UI[2], UI[3] and UI[8] must be ON
Check UO[1] Command enabled and UO[2] System ready
Check the mode switch is AUTO and the TP enable switch OFF
Check the Euromap 67 signals from the molding machine

io.desc: Mold open (from molding machine) — typical Euromap 67 assignment
Safety devices of molding machine closed — typical Euromap 67 assignment
Molding machine in automatic — typical Euromap 67 assignment
Molding machine E-stop OK — typical Euromap 67 assignment

sequence.name: Power-up and servo ready
sequence.desc: Breaker on, controller boots, E-stop chains reset, servos turn on. With UOP enabled the controller reports it is ready to the cell PLC.
sequence.ends: System ready and command enabled are ON
hw: E-stop chains (SOP, TP, external EES, fence EAS) open the servo power directly, outside the program

sequence.name: Program select and start
sequence.desc: The PLC selects the unload program by RSR or PNS and pulses START or PROD_START; the robot acknowledges.

sequence.name: Wait at perch
sequence.desc: Robot waits outside the mold area with the gripper empty, telling the molding machine the mold area is free.

sequence.name: Enter mold and pick
sequence.desc: Mold area free goes OFF, robot moves into the open mold, aligns with the part and turns on vacuum or closes the gripper; it then enables ejector forward to push the part into the gripper.

sequence.name: Retract and release the mold
sequence.desc: Ejector back is enabled, robot leaves the mold area and sets mold area free so the molding machine can close.
sequence.ends: Robot clear of the mold, mold area free ON

sequence.name: Place part
sequence.desc: Robot moves to the conveyor, waits for it to be ready, and releases the part.

sequence.name: Return to perch
sequence.desc: Robot returns to perch and waits for the next mold open.

checks.name: Daily checks
checks.why: Catch damage and dirt before they cause alarms.
steps: Look over the robot, gripper and cables for damage, cracks or leaks
Check the teach pendant cable is not twisted or crushed
Check the air supply pressure for the gripper
After the shift: send the robot home, clean it, clear dust from the cabinet vents and lock the cabinet door

checks.name: One month after start-up
checks.why: Early fan failures show up in the first month.
steps: Check every cabinet fan turns normally

checks.name: Every 6 months
checks.why: Keeps the cabinet cool and proves the safety circuit still works.
steps: Clean dirt and dust from inside the cabinet, the fans and the transformer (power locked out)
Test the safety function: press each E-stop and open the gate, and check the robot stops with the expected alarm
Inspect the door gasket and check there is no gap when locked
Check the cable entrance seal

checks.name: Pulsecoder battery replacement
checks.why: A dead encoder battery loses all axis positions (BZAL) and forces re-mastering.
steps: Replace at the interval in the mechanical unit manual, or as soon as BLAL / SRVO-065 or UO[9] battery alarm appears
Keep the controller powered ON and press the E-stop while changing it
Replace the whole pack, then check no BZAL appears

checks.name: Main board memory battery
checks.why: Backs up programs and settings on the main board.
steps: Replace every 4 years
Take a full backup to USB first

checks.name: Greasing
checks.why: Reducers and gears need fresh grease at the intervals in the mechanical unit manual.
steps: Use FANUC greasing kit A05B-1142-K021 / K023
On these kits, pushing the plunger 2.5 mm delivers about 1 ml of grease
Follow the per-axis amounts and intervals in the LR Mate 200iD mechanical unit manual (B-83494EN, chapter 7)

checks.name: Backups
checks.why: A restore is the fastest recovery from a board or memory failure.
steps: Back up all files and an image backup to USB after any program change
Avoid frequent automatic backups to the internal F-ROM (FRA:), which wears it out; use external storage

checks.name: Mastering after BZAL, pulse mismatch or a motor change
checks.why: The robot's zero positions must be re-established or every point will be off.
steps: Set $MASTER_ENB to 1
SYSTEM > Master/Cal: jog each axis to its mastering marks (release brakes manually if needed, with the arm supported)
Run the mastering method, confirm, then CALIBRATE and press DONE
Touch up a reference point to confirm

reference.name: LR Mate 200iD specifications
notes: Motion ranges are total travel per the datasheet; check the robot's own limits on its system variables.

reference.name: R-30iB Mate Plus cabinet
reference.intro: What each unit does, and the fuses mentioned in the maintenance manual.
rows: CPU, memory, operator panel control; status and 7-segment LEDs; fuse FUSE1
Drives the motors; Pulsecoder, brake, overtravel and hand-broken signals; fuses FS1, FS2 (overtravel), FS3 (regeneration)
Converts AC input to the controller's DC supplies
Controls the E-stop system; terminals for safety and external on/off signals
Terminal block TBOP20 for external E-stop (EES) and fence (EAS); fuse FUSE3 (pendant power)
Board slots and cabinet fan connections
Main board memory backup, replace every 4 years
notes: Fuse ratings are not given in the sourced pages; read them off the boards or the full manual.

reference.name: Stop signal screen
reference.intro: STATUS > Stop Signal shows which safety input is active (read-only).
notes: Use this screen first: it tells you which circuit to chase.

reference.name: Reading alarms
rows: Alarms of PAUSE severity or worse since the last reset
MENU > ALARM > HIST; F5 HELP shows detail
1 hides NONE/WARN, 2 hides resets, 3 hides both from history
notes: Don't relax overload (OVC) protection parameters to clear an alarm; find the load or binding.

reference.name: Starting programs from a PLC
reference.intro: UOP lets the molding machine or cell PLC run the robot.
rows: Robot Service Request: each RSR input starts its own program
Program Number Select: binary program number on PNS1–8, then PNSTROBE
Program number from the cell, start by PROD_START
notes: UOP signal numbers here are FANUC's standard layout; confirm the rack/slot assignment on your I/O config screen.

devices.func: CPU, memory and operator panel control; status LEDs; FUSE1 on board
6-axis servo amplifier: motors, Pulsecoders, brakes, overtravel and hand-broken inputs
Power supply unit: AC input to controller DC supplies
Emergency stop control; safety and external on/off terminals
TBOP20: external E-stop (EES) and fence (EAS) terminals; FUSE3 pendant power
E-stop board fuse: teach pendant power (board LED red when blown)
Board slots and fan connections FAN0/FAN1
Discharge resistor, about 6.5 Ω, for regenerative energy
Optional process I/O board on I/O Link: UOP and cell signals
Main board memory backup battery, replace every 4 years

defects.name: Dropped part
defects.looks: Part falls during transfer or is found in the mold or under the robot.
isolate: Watch the vacuum or part-present signal through the move
Check whether drops happen on fast moves only

causes.cause: Worn or torn vacuum cup, leaking hose

causes.fix: Check regulator and pressure switch setting

causes.cause: Acceleration too high for the grip
causes.fix: Lower acceleration on the transfer move

causes.cause: Part still hot and soft, or oily mold release
causes.fix: Adjust cooling time; check mold release use

defects.name: Marks or scratches from the gripper
defects.looks: Dents, scuffs or cup rings on the part surface.
isolate: Compare marks with the cup or finger positions

causes.fix: Use softer cup material; clean or replace

causes.cause: Gripper pressing the part too hard at pick
causes.fix: Reteach the pick point slightly back

defects.name: Part not released from the mold
defects.looks: Part stays on the core or ejector pins; robot reports no part present or collides on the next cycle.
isolate: Check whether ejection completed before the pick

causes.cause: Ejector forward not enabled or too short
causes.fix: Check the Euromap 67 ejector handshake and stroke

causes.cause: Sticking from undercuts, low draft or a worn surface
causes.fix: Polish or repair the mold; adjust mold release
Wait for ejector forward position before gripping

defects.name: Inconsistent part placement
defects.looks: Parts land off-position or rotated on the conveyor or in the box.
isolate: Check whether the error is constant (frame/TCP) or random (grip slip)

causes.cause: Tool frame (TCP) or user frame wrong after a gripper change
causes.fix: Re-teach the tool frame and check the user frame

causes.cause: Mastering lost after a battery or motor change
causes.fix: Verify mastering against a reference point

defects.name: Cycle time longer than standard
defects.looks: Molding machine waits for the robot; production rate drops.
isolate: Compare robot wait times at perch and in the mold

causes.cause: Robot running below 100% override or with extra waits
causes.fix: Check override and remove unnecessary waits

causes.cause: Inefficient path (fine terminations where CNT would do)
causes.fix: Use continuous (CNT) termination outside the mold
